lines.cap: Someone collapses on a busy street. Twenty people walk past.
lines.say: Someone collapses on a busy street. Twenty people walk past.

lines.cap: It's called the bystander effect. The more people watching, the less each one feels it's their job.
lines.say: It's called the bystander effect. The more people watching, the less each one feels it's their job.

lines.cap: In a famous 1968 study, people on their own nearly always went to help. In a group, far fewer did.
lines.say: In a famous 1968 study, people on their own nearly always went to help. In a group, far fewer did.

lines.cap: So if it ever happens, don't shout, somebody call an ambulance.
lines.say: So if it ever happens, don't shout, somebody call an ambulance.

lines.cap: Point at one person. You, in the red jacket. Call an ambulance.
lines.say: Point at one person. You, in the red jacket. Call an ambulance.

lines.cap: Then pick another. You. Find a defibrillator.
lines.say: Then pick another. You. Find a defibrillator.

lines.cap: Now they're not part of a crowd. They're responsible. And people almost always do it.
lines.say: Now they're not part of a crowd. They're responsible. And people almost always do it.

lines.cap: If the person isn't breathing normally, push hard and fast in the centre of the chest, until help arrives.

lines.cap: Save this. One sentence could save a life.
